edits.text: PARTIES. This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement is between Northwind Capital and Oakstone Ventures, effective as of the date of the last signature below. Each party may act as a disclosing party or receiving party.

1. PURPOSE. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction (the “Purpose”) and may disclose Confidential Information to one another. Neither party is obligated to disclose information or proceed with any transaction. No license or other intellectual property right is granted except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.

2. CONFIDENTIALITY. “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information disclosed by or on behalf of a party in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is identified as confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential, including analyses reflecting that information. The receiving party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and protect it with at least reasonable care. Disclosure is permitted only to its employees, officers, directors, and professional advisers who need to know for the Purpose and are subject to confidentiality duties at least as protective as this Agreement. The receiving party is responsible for their compliance. Confidential Information excludes information the receiving party can demonstrate was lawfully known without restriction before disclosure, becomes public without breach of this Agreement, is lawfully received from a third party without a confidentiality duty, or is independently developed without use of Confidential Information. If disclosure is legally required, the receiving party may disclose only the portion legally required and shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt advance notice and reasonable assistance, at the disclosing party’s expense, in seeking protective treatment. These obligations continue for three years after each disclosure; information qualifying as a trade secret remains protected for as long as it so qualifies under applicable law.

3. TERM; RETURN OF INFORMATION. This Agreement remains in effect for twenty-four months from its effective date unless either party terminates it earlier by written notice. Termination or expiration does not affect obligations concerning information previously disclosed. Upon written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy Confidential Information, including copies and analyses, except records required by law or professional retention obligations and routine backup copies not reasonably accessible in the ordinary course. Retained information remains subject to this Agreement and may not be used for any other purpose.

4. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which damages may be inadequate. The disclosing party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief, subject to applicable law, in addition to any other available remedies.
